mechanisms.description: A trust-extension order extends the trust period on the allotments it covers for a stated number of years. Where that extended period ran out before 1934-06-18, the order's operation ended then by its own terms; any later continuation of the trust was the work of a separate later order or statute with its own lifecycle.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Stated expiry year or date plus the stated number of years (an interval when only the year is stated); TERM only when the whole interval ends before 1934-06-18.

mechanisms.description: IRA sec. 2: "The existing periods of trust placed upon any Indian lands ... are hereby extended and continued until otherwise directed by Congress." By its words it reaches the described class of trust periods existing on 1934-06-18, and an extension order's operative content is such a period. For a member whose period was running on that date, the order's stated end is therefore not a sound TERM end: the period it fixed was continued by statute (coordinator ruling on PD-INDIAN). Whether it was in force on the cutoff turns on whether the tribe came under the IRA (sec. 13 excepts listed Oklahoma tribes; sec. 18 excludes reservations that voted against the Act), on the later instruments for excluded tribes, and on a current record of the trust lands.

For reservations that voted to exclude themselves from the IRA, the Act of June 15, 1935, sec. 3, extended to December 31, 1936 trust periods not already extended past that date; EO 7464 (1936) and annual general orders to EO 10191 (1950), then Interior orders to 1988, extended them further. These decide the open trust members of excluded tribes.

A temporary withdrawal "until" a stated date, in aid of proposed legislation, ends on that date by its own terms (the lands then "become subject to disposal ... without further order"), or earlier if Congress legislates or the President directs otherwise.
A later executive order that names the member (by number or date) and cancels, revokes or supersedes it ends it.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The date of the later order.

mechanisms.description: Coordinator rule P1: an order whose only operative content restores land to the public domain, eliminates land from a reservation or revokes another order is spent on issue; its consequence belongs to the other order's lifecycle or the land's history. A restoration that keeps a retained tract, a reserved right, a purpose restriction or a further direction is not only a restoration.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The order date, or its stated effective date.

mechanisms.description: Coordinator rule P2: an order whose only operative content amends another order merges into the parent on issue; its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.

From 1919-06-30 no new executive-order reservation could be made, and from 1927-03-03 the boundaries of executive-order reservations could be changed only by Act of Congress. A standing reservation order therefore persists until a later executive order (before 1927-03-03) or a statute changes or ends it; these statutes end nothing themselves and tell where to look.

IRA sec. 13: "Sections 2, 4, 7, 16, 17, and 18 of this Act shall not apply" to the listed Oklahoma tribes (Cheyenne, Arapaho, Apache, Comanche, Kiowa, Caddo, Delaware, Wichita, Osage, Kaw, Otoe, Tonkawa, Pawnee, Ponca, Shawnee, Ottawa, Quapaw, Seneca, Wyandotte, Iowa, Sac and Fox, Kickapoo, Pottawatomi, Cherokee, Chickasaw, Choctaw, Creek, Seminole) and affiliated Oklahoma members. For an extension order whose held text names such a tribe in Oklahoma, sec. 2 did not continue the period, the 1935 Act (tied to sec. 18) does not reach it, and the Oklahoma Indian Welfare Act of 1936 does not by its words continue trust periods; the order's own stated end stands.

P8: a statute whose words reimpose or continue the period an order fixed (Capitan Grande 1927, Pala 1936, Yakima 1937, Klamath River 1942; possibly the Kickapoo Act of 1933) makes the order's stated end unsound as a TERM end; the member is open until the statute's reach and end are settled.

A regulation in force on the cutoff that identifies the reservation as the one the order established is a current-law predicate that the order's operative effect, the reservation, was in force on 2026-10-14.

Its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it (P2).

gaps: Held later edges on EO 1598 (EO 1621 revoking part of it, 1912) and EO 744 (EO 1000 of 1908 and EO 1284 of 1911 restoring lands it described) act on the parent order as amended; under P2 they are events of the parent and explain the engine's flags.

Disclosure (P2): its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (EO 709, 711 and 537 are themselves open in this family).
